reasoning: Mississippi is a strongly Republican state, and the only recent Mississippi-specific general-election polling surfaced in the search results suggests Republicans still lead the Senate race. The most usable poll in the results is an April Impact Research survey reported as Hyde-Smith 42%, Colom 39%, and Pinkins 6%, which implies a narrow Republican edge; because that poll is outside the last 45 days, I treated it as supporting context rather than a current-race source and did not rely on unrelated or non-state-specific items.[5]

sources.name: Impact Research (reported by Mississippi Today)
sources.details: Reported in Mississippi Today as showing Cindy Hyde-Smith at 42%, Scott Colom at 39%, and Ty Pinkins at 6%, with 13% undecided; this implies a 3-point Republican lead in the head-to-head matchup.

sources.name: Associated Press
sources.details: AP coverage says the Mississippi Senate race is drawing attention as Democrats try to make the seat more competitive, but the article excerpt provided does not include a usable poll margin.

sources.name: Polymarket
sources.details: A Polymarket market page summarizes recent Mississippi Senate polling as giving Republicans an aggregate lead near 9 points, though it is not itself a state-specific poll and therefore is only contextual.
